name: zoom-in-snap
phrase: zoom in fast
concept: The element snaps from very small to full size in one fast motion, with no bounce. Use it when speed matters more than polish, like a toast or a status chip.

name: expand-in-slow
phrase: expand in slowly
concept: The element grows from almost full size to full size over a long, calm motion. Use it for a deliberate entrance, like a hero panel or a splash section.

name: zoom-in-blast
phrase: zoom in from tiny
concept: The element rushes in from a tiny point straight to full size. Use it for a bold, attention-grabbing entrance, like an alert or a big reveal moment.

name: scale-in-deep
phrase: scale in with a pause
concept: The element stays small and fades in first, then grows to full size. Use it when the viewer should notice the element before it expands.

name: scale-in-soft
phrase: scale in barely
concept: The element scales up from just slightly smaller than its full size, with a soft fade. Use it for a subtle entrance that does not draw much attention.

name: spin-scale-in
phrase: scale in with a half spin
concept: The element grows to full size while it rotates half a turn. Use it for a lively entrance that mixes size change with rotation, like a badge or icon reveal.

name: twist-scale-in
phrase: scale in with a twist
concept: The element grows to full size while it rotates a small amount. Use it for a light entrance with a hint of rotation, gentler than a full spin.

name: scale-in-spiral
phrase: scale in with a spiral turn
concept: The element spins through several turns as it grows, then overshoots slightly before it settles. Use it for a dramatic entrance, like a featured item or a game reward.

name: scale-in-corner-tl
phrase: scale in from the top-left corner
concept: The element grows from its top-left corner instead of its center. Use it when the element sits near a top-left anchor, like a menu that opens from a corner button.

name: scale-in-corner-br
phrase: scale in from the bottom-right corner
concept: The element grows from its bottom-right corner instead of its center. Use it when the element sits near a bottom-right anchor, like a chat bubble that opens from a launcher button.

name: scale-in-corner-tr
phrase: scale in from the top-right corner
concept: The element grows from its top-right corner instead of its center. Use it for a notification or badge that opens from a top-right icon.

name: scale-in-corner-bl
phrase: scale in from the bottom-left corner
concept: The element grows from its bottom-left corner instead of its center. Use it for a tooltip or panel that opens from a bottom-left anchor.

name: scale-in-edge-left
phrase: scale in from the left edge
concept: The element grows outward from its left edge, wider than tall at the start. Use it for a panel or drawer that expands from a left-side trigger.

name: scale-in-edge-top
phrase: scale in from the top edge
concept: The element grows downward from its top edge, flatter than wide at the start. Use it for a dropdown or banner that expands from a top-side trigger.

name: scale-in-focus
phrase: scale in and come into focus
concept: The element starts slightly larger and blurred, then shrinks and sharpens to its resting size. Use it for a camera-focus feel, like a featured photo or preview card.

name: scale-in-hazy
phrase: scale in through a light haze
concept: The element grows from small while a light blur clears. Use it for a soft, dreamy entrance, like an image gallery item or a quote card.

name: zoom-in-blur-snap
phrase: zoom in with a fast blur clear
concept: The element rushes in from small and heavily blurred, then snaps sharp with a slight overshoot. Use it for a punchy, high-energy entrance, like a game notification.

name: scale-in-elastic
phrase: scale in with an elastic settle
concept: The element grows past full size, pulls back, then settles, like a rubber band. Use it for a lively entrance with more spring than a simple pop.

name: scale-in-bounce-double
phrase: scale in with two bounces
concept: The element grows past full size twice before it settles. Use it for a cheerful, bubbly entrance, like a like button or a playful badge.

name: scale-in-bounce-triple
phrase: scale in with three bounces
concept: The element grows past full size three times, each smaller than the last, before it settles. Use it for a rich, toy-like entrance, like a celebratory reward icon.

name: scale-in-skew
phrase: scale in with a horizontal skew
concept: The element grows to full size while it straightens out of a horizontal skew. Use it for a dynamic entrance with a sense of motion, like a sliding card.

name: scale-in-skew-y
phrase: scale in with a vertical skew
concept: The element grows to full size while it straightens out of a vertical skew. Use it for a dynamic entrance that reads as falling into alignment.

name: scale-in-skew-twist
phrase: scale in with a double skew
concept: The element grows to full size while it straightens out of a skew on both axes at once. Use it for a stylized, off-kilter entrance with strong character.

name: iris-in
phrase: open like a camera iris
concept: The element opens from a single point to full size in one quick motion, with a tiny settle at the end. Use it for a lens-like reveal, like a photo viewer or a spotlight.

name: aperture-in
phrase: open like camera blades
concept: The element opens from a tiny point while it rotates a small amount, like aperture blades that swing open. Use it for a mechanical, precise reveal, like a settings dial.

name: unfold-in-horizontal
phrase: unfold open sideways
concept: The element unfolds sideways first, then the height catches up to full size. Use it for a panel or menu that reads as opening like a fan.

name: unfold-in-vertical
phrase: unfold open downward
concept: The element unfolds downward first, then the width catches up to full size. Use it for a dropdown or accordion panel that reads as opening top to bottom.

name: unfold-in-diagonal
phrase: unfold open on a diagonal
concept: The element unfolds wider before it unfolds taller, so the two axes grow at different rates. Use it for a distinctive reveal that feels less mechanical than a straight unfold.

name: scale-in-flip-x
phrase: scale in with a forward flip
concept: The element tips forward from a steep angle and grows to full size as it lands flat. Use it for a card-flip style entrance, like a stat tile or an info card.

name: scale-in-flip-y
phrase: scale in with a side flip
concept: The element turns in from the side at a steep angle and grows to full size as it faces forward. Use it for a card-flip style entrance across a horizontal axis.

name: scale-in-tilt
phrase: scale in with a slight tilt
concept: The element tilts back a small amount and grows to full size as it straightens. Use it for a subtle, three-dimensional pop, gentler than a full flip.

name: scale-in-swoop
phrase: scale in with a swoop
concept: The element swoops down and in from above while it grows and rotates a small amount. Use it for an energetic entrance that combines motion, size, and angle.

name: zoom-in-drift
phrase: zoom in with a slight drift
concept: The element zooms in from small while it drifts sideways a short distance. Use it for a fast entrance with a small sense of direction, like a chat message.

name: scale-in-corner-pull
phrase: scale in and pull from the corner

name: scale-in-squash
phrase: scale in with a squash
concept: The element starts flattened and wide, then squashes and stretches back to its normal shape. Use it for a cartoon-like, tactile entrance, like button press feedback.

name: scale-in-stretch
phrase: scale in with a stretch
concept: The element starts flattened and tall, then stretches and settles back to its normal shape. Use it as the vertical counterpart to a squash entrance.

name: scale-in-rubber
phrase: scale in like rubber
concept: The element grows in and wobbles between wide and tall a few times before it settles. Use it for a stretchy entrance with more character than a plain bounce.

name: scale-in-vortex
phrase: scale in through a blurred vortex
concept: The element spins a full turn and clears from a blur as it grows to full size. Use it for a dramatic, high-energy entrance, like a loading result or a big reveal.

name: scale-in-roll
phrase: scale in with a roll
concept: The element rolls in through a half turn as it grows to full size, with no blur. Use it for a clean rotating entrance, simpler than a vortex.

name: scale-in-crisp
phrase: scale in and sharpen crisply
concept: The element grows a small amount while a light blur clears quickly. Use it for a fast, clean entrance with just a touch of focus effect.

name: scale-in-wide
phrase: scale in from wide
concept: The element starts short and wide, then narrows and settles to its normal size. Use it for a horizontal-feeling entrance, like a banner or a wide button.

name: scale-in-tall
phrase: scale in from tall
concept: The element starts narrow and tall, then widens and settles to its normal size. Use it for a vertical-feeling entrance, like a sidebar item or a tall card.

name: scale-in-diamond
phrase: scale in as a diamond
concept: The element grows in as a diamond shape and rotates into a square as it settles. Use it for a distinctive, geometric entrance, like an achievement icon.

name: scale-in-corner-spin
phrase: scale in and spin from the corner

name: scale-in-billow
phrase: scale in like a soft billow
concept: The element grows slowly from a heavy blur that clears in gradual stages. Use it for a soft, smoke-like entrance, like a background element or an ambient card.

name: scale-in-defocus

concept: The element starts larger than normal and heavily blurred, then shrinks and sharpens to its resting size. Use it for a dramatic focus-pull entrance, stronger than a light focus effect.

name: scale-in-skew-snap
phrase: scale in with a skew snap
concept: The element grows in from a strong skew, overshoots past straight, then settles flat. Use it for a fast, energetic entrance with a whip-like feel.

name: scale-in-pinwheel
phrase: scale in like a pinwheel
concept: The element spins one and a half turns as it grows from a tiny point. Use it for a whimsical, toy-like entrance, like a pinwheel or a spinning coin.

name: scale-in-aperture-close

concept: The element starts larger than normal, narrows down sharply, then springs back to its resting size. Use it for a shutter-like entrance that snaps through a pinch point.

name: scale-in-corner-fold
phrase: scale in and unfold from the corner
concept: The element grows from its top-left corner while it rotates and overshoots slightly. Use it for a rich corner entrance that combines an anchor point with a fold-like turn.
